stem:
Meena and her grandmother are hanging washed clothes to dry on the terrace of their house in Jaipur. The sun is shining strongly.

They have four cotton shirts of the same material and thickness, each a different colour.

Grandmother says: “In summer we should wear the shirt that reflects most of the Sun’s heat so we feel cooler.”

Which shirt should Meena choose to stay coolest on a hot summer afternoon?

options.text: the black shirt, because dark surfaces absorb heat quickly
the white shirt, because light surfaces reflect most of the heat falling on them
the dark blue shirt, because darker colours keep body heat trapped
any of the shirts, because colour only changes how a shirt looks, not how hot it feels

teacher.key_rationale: Light-coloured (white) surfaces reflect most of the heat falling on them, so the white shirt keeps the wearer coolest in strong summer sun. Dark colours (black, dark blue) absorb more heat, and colour does affect heat gain, not just appearance.
